newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto seeks ownership ceiling on listed firms.
newsitem.headline: Suharto seeks ownership ceiling on listed firms.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto said on Tuesday the largest single shareholding in private companies listed on local bourses should not exceed 15 percent.

The minister of cooperatives and small business, Subiyakto Tjaakrawerdaya, quoted Suharto as saying that in his view an individual shareholder in a private company going public should not hold more than 15 percent of the equity.
"The control should not exceed 15 percent. It should be a maximum of 15 percent and other people should be able to get a stake," he quoted the president as saying following a meeting with Suharto.
The minister quoted Suharto as calling for "equitability" in shareholdings.
This was the president's commitment to the people, he added.

The minister declined to name any specific company, but it appeared from the context he was referring to the issue of Indonesia's largest car maker, Astra International, which had been the target of a bidding war in recent weeks.
Tjakrawerdaya gave no indication that the government had any plans to restrict shareholdings.
But he quoted Suharto as saying he would "encourage" other investors to buy shares in companies that were under the control of one group for equitability.
